rationales: Atomic radius is conventionally half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded identical atoms.
Atomic size is a general term, not the specific term defined here.
An ionic bond is a type of chemical bond, not a measure of atomic size.
Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron from an atom.
NaCl is an ionic compound that dissolves readily in water.
KBr is an ionic compound that dissolves in water.
C₆H₆ (benzene) is nonpolar and is insoluble in water.
MgCl₂ is an ionic compound that dissolves in water.
0.03% is not the stated proportion of chlorine in ocean water.
0.9% is lower than the usual stated chlorine proportion in ocean water.
7.8% is much higher than the stated chlorine proportion in ocean water.
The chlorine content is approximately 1.8% according to the stated value.
Density is mass per unit volume, not moles of solute per unit volume.
Percentage expresses a proportion, not moles per dm³.
Molarity is the number of moles of solute per dm³ of solution.
Dilution is the process of lowering a solution’s concentration.
Melting changes a solid into a liquid.
Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.
Condensation changes a gas into a liquid.
Freezing changes a liquid into a solid.
An ionic bond involves electron transfer and electrostatic attraction.
A coordinate bond forms when one atom supplies both shared electrons.
System energy is not a type of chemical bond.
A pure covalent bond forms when similar atoms share electrons equally.
Milk is a colloid and is classified as a heterogeneous mixture.
Ink may be treated as a colloidal mixture and can also be heterogeneous.
Milk of magnesia is a suspension and is a heterogeneous mixture.
Sugar solution is a homogeneous mixture; however, both milk and milk of magnesia make the question ambiguous.
450 °C is too low for sodium chloride’s melting point.
1413 °C is not the melting point of sodium chloride.
Sodium chloride melts at about 801 °C, conventionally rounded to 800 °C.
1000 °C is higher than sodium chloride’s melting point.
2.7 is below fluorine’s electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
3.0 is below fluorine’s electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
3.2 is below fluorine’s electronegativity on the Pauling scale.
Fluorine’s electronegativity is about 4.0 on the Pauling scale.
160 pm is too small for the stated atomic size of sodium.
162 pm is too small for the stated atomic size of sodium.
185 pm is close but is not the commonly tabulated value in this question.
The commonly stated atomic radius of sodium is 186 pm.
Carbon-12 makes up about 98.9% of naturally occurring carbon.
96.6% is below the natural abundance of carbon-12.
99.7% is above the natural abundance of carbon-12.
97.6% is below the natural abundance of carbon-12.
Chlorine does not have one valence electron.
Chlorine does not have two valence electrons.
Chlorine has more than five valence electrons.
Chlorine has seven valence electrons in its outer shell.
H₂O contains three atoms per molecule.
H₂ contains two atoms per molecule, so it is not triatomic.
O₃ contains three atoms per molecule.
CO₂ contains three atoms per molecule.
Electrons are not the characteristic particles produced in U-235 fission.
Protons are not the characteristic particles produced in U-235 fission.
U-235 fission releases neutrons along with fission fragments and energy.
Potassium is not the expected answer among the listed fission products.
Mendeleev’s table was not arranged by electronic configuration.
Mendeleev arranged elements primarily in order of increasing atomic mass.
Atomic number was the basis of the modern periodic table, not Mendeleev’s original table.
Completion of subshells was not the basis of Mendeleev’s table.
